sentences.text: Laevisuchus was a small, bipedal meat-eating dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Scientists know this creature from a collection of neck bones and a single back bone.
One of these bones has a top arch that is much wider and longer than the central part, creating a top-heavy look.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a height of 90 centimeters and weighed roughly 30 kilograms.
Charles Alfred Matley found the fossils near Jabalpur in central India, and Huene and Matley described them in 1933.
Most of the original material was lost until researchers found a neck bone again in 2012.
Modern studies place Laevisuchus within the Noasauridae family.
A 2004 analysis identified it as an abelisauroid based on long extensions on the vertebrae, holes in the center, and low triangular spines.
It lived about 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous on the Indian subcontinent.
The fossil record for this era spans from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
